---
title: "Coherence of pairwise threshold decisions"
subtitle: "3.10 · after Kline, Rose and Walters (2024), §V.E"
description: "Pairwise threshold decisions can conflict with each other, even when no strict cycle occurs."
---

Thresholding each pair separately states a direction whenever its error probability falls strictly below $\tau$. Compare those isolated pair choices with coherent grade reports across triples of firms.

```{=html}

```

## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **Race λ .25.** Naive thresholding states 1,575 directions and leaves 32,773 of 147,440 triples with two withheld pairs and one stated.
- **Race λ .10.** The two-withheld conflict count is 24,278.
- **Race λ .50.** Reporting more directions reduces two-withheld conflicts to 15,107.
- **Race λ .75.** Conflicts fall further to 3,108 without any strict directed cycle.
- **Race λ .25, card blocks.** The card withholds 575 confident pairs and states 324 directions above τ to restore coherence without a grade cap.
- **Gender λ 1.00.** All 4,656 pairs are stated, leaving 1 directed cycle that precludes a coherent grade report.

<details>
<summary>Transitivity and archived cards</summary>

A shared grade leaves the direction between two firms unranked, and sharing a grade is transitive: withholding A–B and B–C puts all three firms in one grade, contradicting a stated direction on A–C. Threshold decisions and archived KRW cards are evaluated here under the released signed-target probabilities.

</details>
